newsitem.title: QATAR: Trade subdued on Qatar's new bourse.
newsitem.headline: Trade subdued on Qatar's new bourse.

text.p: Trade was subdued on the 10-day-old Doha Securities Market in the week to Thursday with an average of two to three deals a day, brokers said.

"Most shares are in demand, but few shares are being offered to satisfy demand," Mazin al-Shakarchi, assistant general manager of treasury and investments at the Commercial Bank of Qatar, told Reuters.
The CBQ's 17-share index inched up to 131.76 points from 131.17 points last week. The exchange has not set up its own official index yet.
A total of 14,260 shares worth 749,421 riyals ($205,884) changed hands in the week, the DSM said. Five shares rose, two fell and 10 were unchanged.
The biggest gainer was Qatar General Insurance which began rebounding after losing 270 riyals the previous week as it went ex-dividend. It gained 45 riyals to close at 420.
Other gainers included the CBQ, which rose five riyals to 310 and Qatar International Islamic Bank, which jumped eight riyals to 94.50.
Qatar Industrial Manufacturing Company picked up two riyals to 62 and Qatar Islamic Bank crept up one riyal to 137.
Losers included Qatar Leisure, which lost two riyals to 45, and Qatar Flour Mills, which shed one riyal to 306.
